creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Tracks GitHub #140. Not a gate on the current bugfix work - raised here so it stops living only as an issue.

The current suite in `core/testing` is example-based and good at what it covers. What it cannot cover is the combinatorial space where evaluator-semantics bugs live: scoping x call depth x error paths x closures. #137 was exactly that shape - invisible until someone writes the precise program, trivial for a generator to find.

The invariants #140 names map directly onto bugs we are working right now: a handler evaluates in the scope of the catch site at any propagation depth; locals never leak across frames; an unhandled error from depth N surfaces with message and stack intact; closures see the environment they captured.

Its metamorphic oracles are the interesting part - inlining a call must not change output, wrapping an expression in an identity fn must not change scoping, adding an unused local must change nothing. Each would have caught #137 alone. They are also the only cheap way to *prove* whatever we decide in a_25TdzYuMr (error value identity) holds at depths example tests never reach.

Open questions live on the issue: CI budget and whether to split nightly-deep from shallow-on-PR; whether the generator targets the AST (shrinks better) or source text (also exercises the parser); how much of this `rad check` should catch statically instead.

`pgregory.net/rapid` does generation and shrinking well; `testing/quick` is the stdlib fallback.
title: Build the property-based harness for evaluator semantics (GH #140)
